title: What Is CSS?
description: Understand CSS as a rule-based styling language: master selector-declaration syntax, property-value pairs, linking stylesheets via <link rel="stylesheet">, and the separation of concerns.

objectives.statement: Identify and author the anatomy of a CSS rule, including selector, declaration block, property, and value.
Style HTML elements by defining color, font-size, and background properties in a stylesheet.

content.title: Separating Structure from Presentation
content.hook: HTML provides the raw structure of the web, but CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) brings it to life with typography, color, spacing, and layout.
content.context: CSS works by matching selectors to DOM elements and applying declaration blocks containing property-value pairs.
goals: Understand the anatomy of a CSS rule (selector { property: value; }).
Apply fundamental presentation rules (color, background-color, font-size).
Appreciate the architectural value of keeping styling separate from markup.

content.title: Anatomy of a CSS Rule
content.description: A CSS rule consists of a Selector ('h1'), an opening curly brace '{', Declarations containing a Property ('color') and Value ('#2563eb') terminated by a semicolon ';', and a closing curly brace '}'.

content.prompt: Look at the following CSS rule. If a developer forgets the semicolon after `color: red`, what happens to the subsequent `font-size` declaration?
options: The browser automatically fixes the missing semicolon and applies both styles normally
The browser treats 'color: red font-size: 18px' as an invalid declaration, discarding both properties
The color rule is applied, but font-size is ignored
The entire web page fails to render with a fatal crash

validation.expected: The browser treats 'color: red font-size: 18px' as an invalid declaration, discarding both properties

feedback.correct: Exact! In CSS syntax, semicolons delineate individual declarations. Without a semicolon, the parser sees an unrecognized compound value and discards the declaration.
feedback.incorrect: CSS parsers rely on semicolons to delimit property-value pairs. Omitting a semicolon causes the parser to combine them into an invalid declaration and drop it.

content.title: Style a Welcome Banner
content.prompt:
Write CSS rules to style the page elements:
1. Give `h1` a `color` of `#1e3a8a` and `font-size` of `24px`.
2. Give `p` a `color` of `#4b5563`.
3. Give `.banner` a `background-color` of `#f3f4f6`.
content.starterCode:
Welcome to Forge

Learn web development through active engineering practice.

testCases.description: h1 must have a styled blue color (#1e3a8a / rgb(30, 58, 138))
p must have a styled gray color (#4b5563 / rgb(75, 85, 99))

feedback.correct: Brilliant! You've authored valid CSS rules targeting elements and classes with clean property-value declarations.
feedback.incorrect: Check your selectors and property values. Ensure h1, p, and .banner each have closing curly braces and terminating semicolons.

hints.content: Target elements directly with their tag name (e.g. `h1 { color: #1e3a8a; font-size: 24px; }`).
Target classes with a leading dot (e.g. `.banner { background-color: #f3f4f6; }`).

content.prompt: Why is keeping presentation styles inside external CSS files considered superior to writing inline `style="..."` attributes on every HTML tag?

feedback.correct: Spot on! External CSS promotes maintainability, enables caching across multiple pages, adheres to the separation of concerns, and drastically reduces repetition.
feedback.incorrect: Think about maintainability, multi-page styling consistency, and caching.

content.title: Key Takeaways: CSS Basics
takeaways: A CSS rule consists of a selector and a declaration block.
Declarations are property: value; pairs separated by semicolons.
Element selectors match tags (p, h1), while class selectors match .classname.
External stylesheets separate structural content from visual presentation.
